articles.title: ‘You can’t bring in robots’: the leather firm handmaking everything from wallets to cigar cases
articles.summary: In the third article in a series on high-end British manufacturing, we visit the Ettinger factory in Walsall. ‘Our town is making jeans again’: reviving jobs and skills in Wales. From feathers to pet portraits, Rolls-Royce rides high on custom craze.
body: “It is all down to attention to detail and everything we do is based around that.”

Gary Billingham is demonstrating how the 28 pieces which make up an Ettinger wallet are cut from leather using a hydraulic press by the small team at one of Walsall’s last remaining leather goods factories. The edges of the pieces are thinned down so they are ready to be turned, glued and stitched together by hand.

Billingham has been at the factory near Birmingham since the 1980s, when “there were three pages in the Yellow Pages” business directory listing leather factories in the West Midlands town. “They were everywhere. It has gone from that to about five factories. It is more like a cottage industry.”
About 20 people, mostly women, work carefully and precisely in Ettinger’s factory – a site of leather goods production since the 1890s – with a handful more doing work from home.
points: In the third article in a series on high-end British manufacturing, we visit the Ettinger factory in Walsall. ‘Our town is making jeans again’: reviving jobs and skills in Wales.

articles.title: The hill I will die on: The email sign-off is archaic - it needs to go. No regards, Tom | Tom Gill
articles.summary: The torture of the inbox is made insufferably worse by the dated cliches at the beginning and end. Enough! If email were a person, it would be an adult dressed in a teenager’s clothes, desperately trying to stay relevant.
body: Whereas other forms of communication have long since dispensed with unnecessary textual tassels, email communication styles still lean closer to telegram than a text. Since I last checked, almost no one relishes receiving a new email – unless it’s informing you of a significant cash windfall that means you can, in fact, now quit your job and stop using it altogether. Yet, for some reason, many people start their responses with “Thank you for your email!” I would put this forward as one of the least convincing sentences in the English language.

At the other end of the page is one of the most common yet totally unnecessary habits of the digital age: the email signoff. For those who haven’t yet realised, I’m here to tell you that you don’t need to sign your name at the end of an email – I can already see it’s from you. I know your name. Outlook has gone to extraordinary lengths to tell me your name. It’s in my inbox, the “from” field and the thread, and I probably begrudgingly addressed my last email directly to you.
points: The torture of the inbox is made insufferably worse by the dated cliches at the beginning and end.
If email were a person, it would be an adult dressed in a teenager’s clothes, desperately trying to stay relevant.

articles.title: Carving out a greener future: how the Swiss ski resort of Laax is meeting the climate crisis head on
articles.summary: Gondolas on demand, electric piste-grooming and chemical-free snow cannons – how Laax is ‘greenstyling’ its future. It’s the worst ski resort nightmare: hillsides of shaggy yellow grass streaked with slush under a leaden sky that’s coughing up sleet.
body: Not everywhere, of course. Only lower altitudes are seeing such disasters. Higher up, normal service continues. I’m in the Swiss resort of Laax, where most of the slopes are at about 2,000 metres, lofty enough to be snow-secure, for now. The halfpipe is busy with dudes in baggy trousers and headphones nonchalantly practising their double corks. On the traditional pistes there are four-year-olds who could probably ski before they could walk. And then – Switzerland has its wacky side – three young men in first-world-war greatcoats on antique wooden skis propel themselves with rough-hewn quarter-staves.

Is all this destined to disappear, perhaps in our children’s lifetimes? To put it in stark, white and black terms: are ski resorts in the same predicament as oil-dependent desert states, watching their one key source of wealth dwindle and disappear?

articles.title: Greg Wise on how he and Emma Thompson coped with failed IVF: ‘We hit an existential crisis – she was not a proper woman and I was not a proper man’
articles.summary: Their hopes of having a second child were dashed. Two decades on, the actor remembers the grief and pain of that time. “I’m afraid this cycle has not been successful.” Emma and I cannot catch each other’s eye. We sit mute in our grief in the silence of the IVF doctor’s office.
body: Each cycle, each time we sat in that office, we had to ignore our grief and concentrate wholeheartedly and positively on our next attempt. We didn’t access any help over this time. We didn’t seek out counselling as a couple. I had no knowledge of how to process my grief – compounded month on month. Further cycles, more drugs, more fertility hormones, more ovarian hyperstimulation, injections, scans, blood tests came and went, all proving unsuccessful. I supported all wholeheartedly, but Emma was devastated by her inability to conceive again. In her mind, she had failed and could not forgive herself for that failure. And nothing I could say would change her point of view.
Her deep grief took her away. I had to deny mine. Try to comfort her rather than myself. Such is the lot of the self-appointed saviour.

articles.title: From Elizabeth Taylor to Kim Kardashian and Kris Jenner: The Starry History of the Scorpio Cape
articles.summary: At the “All’s Fair” premiere in Rome, Kris Jenner paid homage to Elizabeth Taylor, Grace Kelly, and Kim Kardashian with a piece of fashion history.
body: Kim Kardashian and Kris Jenner have a shared affinity for archival fashion and high-octane glamour, with an increasing penchant for mother-daughter twinning. But their latest red carpet outing came with a particularly storied piece of Hollywood history, involving Elizabeth Taylor, Grace Kelly, and a certain astrological sign of the moment.

At the Rome Film Festival last night, where Kardashian was celebrating the season two premiere of Ryan Murphy’s legal drama All’s Fair, Jenner arrived in a sweeping black velvet hooded cape, its ivory silk lining framing her face and glittering scorpions embroidered across the chest. She wore it with long white gloves and a floor-length white gown underneath.
The striking design was a homage to a Tiziani Roma creation worn by Elizabeth Taylor in 1969, when the actor attended Princess Grace of Monaco’s 40th birthday celebrations.

articles.title: 18 of the Best ’90s Movies to Revisit This Fall
articles.summary: From Lynchian classics to Sofia Coppola fever dreams, here are the ’90s films worth watching—for the first or 10th time—today.
body: Listen—they just made better movies in the ’90s. While today’s cinema listings are crammed with sequels and remakes, with the watching experience couched in discourse and then discourse about the discourse, the best ’90s films were for the most part true originals. To add to that, a good film resulted in a long relationship with it. Rather than watching something once, plugging in a pithy Letterboxd review, and forgetting about it within a week, ’90s films existed on love-worn VHS tapes to be watched on repeat until the outfits and most quotable one-liners remained stamped onto the brain forever.

While I’m not going to list every single ’90s movie worth watching—that would take an age; British Vogue has a separate list for ’90s films for fashion lovers —there are definitely a few stand-out classics worth returning to. Below, the best ’90s movies to watch (or rewatch) for some much-needed escapism and entertainment.

articles.title: Inside the Couture Council Luncheon, Where Diane von Furstenberg Was Celebrated as a “Force of Nature”
articles.summary: The 2026 Couture Council Award was presented to designer, author, and philanthropist, Diane von Furstenberg at Gotham Hall in New York. Fashion industry veterans, emerging designers, and supporters alike showed up wearing signature DVF prints.
body: “All my life, I wanted to be the woman in charge—and then I became a woman in charge of a little dress,” Diane von Furstenberg told an audience at Gotham Hall as she accepted the 2026 Couture Council Award. Of course, those familiar with the designer’s story knew she was referencing the title of her 2024 documentary, Woman in Charge, which chronicles her illustrious life and journey to building a global fashion empire.

More than 50 years after she created her groundbreaking wrap dress, the design still resonates, as evidenced by the room full of people dressed in the silhouette on Thursday at FIT/The Museum at FIT’s annual Couture Council luncheon. Martha Stewart, Narciso Rodriguez, Nicole Miller, Linda Fargo, Fern Mallis, Erin Walsh, and Candace Bushnell were among those who turned out in style to celebrate an industry icon.

articles.title: Lauren Santo Domingo Brought a Stylish Crowd to Colombia to Fete the Four Seasons Cartagena
articles.summary: Colombian culture and fashion took center stage at a weekend-long celebration for the newly opened Four Seasons Cartagena.
body: Summer wardrobes may be packed away until next year, but this past weekend, a fashionable group traded crisp air and trench coats for tropics-friendly resortwear at the Four Seasons Cartagena. Guests—including Lauren and Andrés Santo Domingo; Alejandro and Charlotte Santo Domingo; Andrea and Tatiana Casiraghi; chef Mario Carbone and Cait Bailey Carbone; artist Olympia Scarry; designers Johanna Ortiz, Danielle Frankel Hirsch, Conner Ives, and Annie Doble; and entrepreneur Jen Rubio—took over the sprawling property’s 131 rooms for a multi-day celebration of Colombian culture.

“The city has a sense of magical realism,” remarked Lauren Santo Domingo, citing Cartagena’s prodigal son, Gabriel García Márquez. “The first time I came here, I really felt like I was transported and I was somewhere different, unlike anywhere I’ve ever been: every corner on every street, every balcony, is covered in bougainvillea.”

articles.title: I Asked 8 Chefs to Name the Best Jarred Pasta Sauce — This Is the One They Swear By
articles.summary: Pasta is one of my favorite foods, and what really makes it is the sauce. A good sauce can often require simmering the ingredients for hours until all the flavors have melded. But sometimes we don’t have time for that.
body: So when we need something simple, quick, and easy to grab, jarred sauces can be a kitchen hero. I’ve tried many on the market, but was curious to learn which ones professional chefs give the stamp of approval. So I asked 8 chefs: What is the best jarred marinara sauce? One clearly swept the board but there were a few other favorites. Here are the jarred sauces you should stock your pantry shelves with.

The majority of the chefs (6 out of 8!) chose Rao’s Homemade as their top pick, praising it for being a great base for dishes like chicken Parmesan, lasagna, pasta puttanesca, and more. (It is Ina Garten’s favorite, too.) Jamie Milne, cookbook author of Everything Delish and busy mom of two, loves how close to homemade it tastes. “Rao’s has that rich, slow-simmered tomato flavor that you would expect from a sauce that’s been cooking on the stove for hours,” Milne said. “It’s made with simple ingredients like Italian tomatoes, olive oil, garlic, onions, and herbs, and you can really taste the difference.”

articles.title: An AI-Created Design Turned Her Empty Corner into a Breakfast Nook
articles.summary: “The breakfast nook was one of those spaces that had so much potential but never felt intentional,” Carmen Murphy shares. Carmen and her boyfriend had moved in together two years ago and had been slowly transforming their apartment.But the couple never really did anything with this space — besides…
body: Because Carmen and her boyfriend were renting, she needed to make sure whatever changes she made to the 11-foot-wide space weren’t permanent but still looked built-in. Instead, Carmen turned to ChatGPT “to come up with some options to use the space to its full potential.”
With ChatGPT’s help, Carmen created a layout that fit the small space perfectly and incorporated her three must-haves for the project — more storage, comfortable seating, and her wine fridge.
“I started by measuring the space over and over to make sure every inch would be used efficiently,” Carmen shares. Once she had a plan, she began researching benches that would fit the wall length.

Carmen found that using an L-shaped corner bench and transforming it into a straight built-in bench was the best fit. “It took a lot of measuring and a bit of creative maneuvering to make sure everything lined up, felt balanced, and looked like it had always been there instead of looking pieced together,” she explains.

articles.title: I Finally Ditched Using Ear Plugs for Sleep, Thanks to This 3-in-1 Device
articles.summary: I thought I’d tried everything when it came to tricks and products to help me get better sleep, from weighted eye masks to “dark showering.” I was convinced that comfy ear plugs were a necessity in my noisy Brooklyn neighborhood — that is, until I realized that some noise can actually be helpful to…
body: Everything changed when I tested out the Canopy Sound Machine + Aroma, and now I can’t remember how I ever slept without it.

The small-but-mighty Canopy Sound Machine + Aroma is a cordless, screenless wellness device that has three distinct functions: It’s a sound machine, night light, and aroma diffuser. It’s designed for all ages, from babies to adults, and has 15 built-in sounds ranging from white noise to nature sounds to instrumental lullabies.

It measures 4 inches by 2 inches by 4 inches, and the device comes with an interior felt aroma pad for adding a few drops of the included lavender float aroma oil, which you can order refills of via a subscription. The attachable clip allows you to lay the machine down, stand it up, hang it, or clip it for use on-the-go. It has dimmable red and white light settings, and the device itself comes in white, gray, tan, green, and purple. It has a battery life of up to 15 hours of continuous use, so you can use it overnight or just use the 30-, 60-, or 90-minute timer settings.

articles.title: Baked Apple Cinnamon French Toast
articles.summary: As a working mom of two, I love a breakfast that feels special without requiring me to spend all morning in the kitchen. This baked apple cinnamon French toast is everything I want in a cozy breakfast: buttery, custardy, sweet, and filled with warm spiced apples.
body: Custardy French toast baked with cinnamon-spiced apples until golden-brown for a cozy breakfast that tastes like apple pie.

As they bake, the apples become tender and their juices add a delicious caramel-like sweetness to every bite. To finish it off, make a quick brown sugar whipped cream that’s light, fluffy, and just sweet enough to complement the warm apples. It’s definitely my favorite part, and my kids agree! Whether you’re hosting a holiday brunch, feeding a crowd, or simply looking for something delicious to make on a slow Sunday morning, this French toast is guaranteed to make breakfast feel a little more special. Serve it warm with a dusting of powdered sugar and a generous spoonful of whipped cream (trust me). A drizzle of maple syrup never hurts, either.

As a professionally trained baker and recipe developer with over a decade of experience in food media, I know a thing or two about creating a delicious breakfast. As a working mom of two, I especially love recipes that can be prepared ahead of time and make a busy morning a little more special.
